evidence: Plan: 'the signed manifest records file-scope: none' — but build_manifest takes only `deps: dict[str, str] | None`; no `file_scope` parameter exists or is named in the plan.

attest.py:707-714: the validity branch is `if deps:` … `else:` whole-HEAD — a third branch reading a `file-scope:` manifest line requires both the line to be written by build_manifest AND a parser like the existing `manifest_deps` to be read by compute_validity; neither is named in the plan.

findings.finding: `build_manifest` has no parameter to carry the file-scope signal, so the plan's claim that 'the signed manifest records file-scope: none' (S2) has no named call-path through which the scope flows from ticket state to the manifest line. With the current interface (`deps: dict[str, str] | None`), an explicitly-none ticket produces `deps={}`, which is byte-identical in the manifest to an undeclared ticket — `compute_validity` cannot distinguish them and the S2 skip cannot be implemented without changing `build_manifest`'s signature.
findings.location: S2 — attestation scoping; src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py:309-375 (build_manifest signature)
scenarios: S2 implementer opens build_manifest, sees no file_scope parameter, and either invents an undocumented convention or returns {} which silently falls through to whole-HEAD freshness, defeating the feature.
compute_validity cannot skip the whole-HEAD check because there is no manifest line to distinguish none-scoped from undeclared-empty attestations.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `file_scope: Literal['undeclared', 'paths', 'none'] | None = None` to `build_manifest`; emit `file-scope: none` when `file_scope == 'none'`; add `manifest_file_scope(manifest) -> str | None` parser; in `compute_validity` replace `else: whole-HEAD` with `elif manifest_file_scope(auth_manifest) == 'none': pass  # explicitly scoped-none; no drift check` before the existing else clause.

findings.finding: All existing signed attestations will have their material fingerprint invalidated the moment the tri-state `file_impact_scope` is added to the fingerprint computation. This is a fleet-wide forced re-review event, but it is not acknowledged as an explicit, justified choice and no rollback or back-out plan is provided. If the deploy must be reverted, attestations re-signed under the new schema are again invalidated, leaving teams in a churn loop.
findings.location: Approach section (material fingerprint paragraph) and S2 child spec
findings.suggested_fix: In the S2 spec, add a 'Migration note': existing attestations whose fingerprint predates the `file_impact_scope` field are treated as `undeclared` scope (no behavioral change). Provide a one-time migration script or a fingerprint-version prefix so old attestations are not immediately invalidated, and document the rollback path (revert the schema change → attestations revert to old fingerprint → re-valid).
